text:
maria: seeing a sustained spike on embeddings -> rerank fanout, rerank lane is saturating and we're tripping the soft limits, users hit 429s. anyone else?
aj: yup noticed it at ~09:10, rerank queue depth shot up 3x. looks like multi-tenant bursts from customer B + long-context reranks.
liam: logs show egress queue latency from embed sidecar to rerank pool, TCP retransmits briefly on one host in eu-west-1. might be a networking blip + backlog.
sophia: is this the same thing as the per-lane admission we rolled out? I thought embed and rerank had separate capacity lanes — why is rerank getting overloaded by embed fanout?
maria: embed fanout still does parallel calls to rerank lane for N candidates. if embed lane doesn't respect rerank admission signals, it overwhelms. we don't currently have a handshake for backpressure across lanes.
aj: proposal: implement a simple sidecar handshake where rerank returns short-circuit advice in headers e.g. X-Rerank-Advice: reject|defer|rate=50 and embed sidecar respects it when dispatching fanout.
liam: +1. also add a soft admission token bucket per-customer on the embed side so a single tenant can't spike global rerank QPS.
sophia: can we avoid a versioned protocol? maybe reuse the existing 429 + Retry-After semantics for quick wins, and add structured header later.
infra-bot: observed 429 bursts from rerank service between 1765432000 and 1765432100, 95th p50 rtt degraded by 240ms on hosts rack-12-eu.
maria: good catch infra-bot. immediate mitigation: reduce embed fanout parallelism from 8 -> 3 for eu-west config and enable per-route slow-path retry with exponential backoff. can someone run a canary?
aj: running canary now on 10% of embed fleet in eu-west. patch: 
```
# embed-sidecar config
fanout_parallelism: 3
respect_rerank_429: true
max_inflight_per_customer: 200
```
liam: after canary we should also enable a rerank admission flag to emit header advice when queue depth > 70%. header format: X-Rerank-Hint: defer; retry-after=1500ms
sophia: long term we should do explicit admission-control RPC between lanes so embed dispatcher can request N tokens from rerank lane before spawning. avoids extra round-trips or failed requests.
maria: agree. short term steps: 1) canary config (aj) 2) add header-emit in rerank (liam) 3) throttle policy per-tenant (sophia) 4) ops run a host-level network health sweep (infra)
aj: canary metrics after 5m: rerank 429s down ~48%, end-to-end p95 reduced ~180ms for canary traffic. rolling to 30%. :thumbsup:
liam: pushed header emit in staging, returns X-Rerank-Hint when queue depth > 65%. sample: `X-Rerank-Hint: defer;retry-after=1200`
sophia: noted cost impact — lowering fanout reduces tokens & GPU utilization, so per-hour cost might drop but latency for some queries goes up. need product signoff on QoS tradeoff for customer B.
maria: I'll loop in product. ops, please monitor for any host with persistent retransmits, we may be seeing a NIC causing partial saturation.
infra-bot: scheduled network sweep job on eu-west rack-12-eu, will report within 30m.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for embed-sidecar canary (10% eu-west) at 1765432325.
aj: rolling to 60% now. keep an eye on multi-tenant fairness metrics, especially tail latencies for small queries.
liam: follow-up: let's add telemetry counters for "cross-lane-rejects" so we can quantify how often rerank forces deferral. helps tune thresholds.
sophia: also add an opt-in per-customer QOS profile so high-value customers can reserve rerank tokens and avoid being throttled during noise.
maria: timeline: quick fixes (this week) = fanout cap + header emit + per-tenant throttle. medium (next sprint) = admission RPC and token reservations. long (Q2) = smarter scheduler and cost-aware routing across regions.
aj: sounds good. I'll create the rollout PR and add a runbook entry for this failure mode.
maria: thanks team. tagging customer-sig to coordinate a communication if we see further user impact.
